scope_reference_policy: Official 2025 MD Standards Statement column, not the legacy 2010 previous-standards column; each parent includes any lettered requirements listed. Original wording resides in official linked PDF; editorial scope_summary in inventory is not accepted source-fidelity proof.

records.scope_summary_editorial: Divide fractions by fractions in context, extending estimation, concrete/visual fraction models, and equations.
Fluently divide multi-digit numbers, choosing efficient strategies or the standard algorithm.
Fluently multiply and divide multi-digit decimals to the thousandths in context.
Identify the common factors and multiples of two whole numbers.

6.NOS.B.4.a: Find greatest common factors of whole numbers bounded by 100
6.NOS.B.4.b: Find least common multiples of whole numbers bounded by 12
6.NOS.B.4.c: Use distributive reasoning to factor sums with whole-number addends bounded by 100

requirements.6.NOS.B.4.c: Factor sums with whole-number addends within 100 by distributivity

records.scope_summary_editorial: Use understanding of rational numbers as positive and negative numbers to describe quantities with opposite directions or values.
Represent rational numbers as points on vertical or horizontal number lines, including points with negative coordinates.
Use perpendicular number lines intersecting at (0,0) to introduce the four quadrants of the Coordinate Plane and represent points with positive and negative coordinates.
Order rational numbers and identify absolute value.
Solve problems in context by graphing points with a shared coordinate in all four quadrants of the Coordinate Plane.
Use ratio language in context to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities, including part-to-part and part-to-whole.
Represent and use unit rates, written as fractions with whole number numerators and denominators, in context.
Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve problems in context with tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number lines, or the Coordinate Plane.
Find a percent of a quantity in context as a rate per 100, including finding the whole given a part and the percent, using tables, tape diagrams, and double number lines.
Write numerical expressions involving whole number exponents and positive rational number bases; evaluate with technology.
Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.
Apply properties of operations to generate equivalent algebraic expressions and to identify when two expressions are equivalent.
Solve problems in context by writing and solving equations and interpreting the solutions in context.

6.AT.C.8.b: Solve one-step equations of forms x+p=q, x−p=q, px=q, x/p=q
Parameters p and q and unknown x are nonnegative rational numbers

requirements.6.AT.C.8.b: x+p=q, x-p=q, px=q and x/p=q; x,p,q nonnegative rational

records.scope_summary_editorial: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint in context; recognize infinitely many solutions and represent them on number lines.
Solve problems in context by writing and solving inequalities and interpreting solution sets in context.

6.AT.C.10.b: Represent one-step inequalities using addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division of an unknown and parameter
Parameters p and q are nonnegative rational numbers

requirements.6.AT.C.10.b: One-step addition, subtraction, multiplication, division inequalities using >=, >, <=, < and p,q nonnegative rational

records.scope_summary_editorial: Use variables to represent two quantities in context that change in relationship to one another.
Find the area of triangles, quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and quadrilaterals.
Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths.
Draw polygons in the Coordinate Plane given vertex coordinates and use coordinates to find side lengths; apply these techniques in context.
Represent three-dimensional figures using nets of rectangles and triangles and use the nets to find surface area to solve problems.
Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.
Use the language of probability to describe the likelihood of possible outcomes and to anticipate variability in data collected from statistical questions.
Explain how a data set collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution described by center, spread, and overall shape.
Recognize that a measure of center summarizes all values with a single number while a measure of variation describes how values vary.
Interpret numerical data in plots on a number line, including line plots, histograms, and box plots.
Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context.

6.DS.B.6.c: Use median and/or mean and interquartile range to describe distributions
Discuss outliers in the context of the data
Do not infer mean absolute deviation from the separate 2010 historical comparison column

requirements.6.DS.B.6.c: 2025 column requires median and/or mean, IQR and outlier context; historical 2010 MAD comparison NOT imported as 2025 requirement
